methodology.metaDescription: Die quellenbasierte Vergleichsmethodik von VPN Advisor: offizielle Dokumente, unabhängige Audits, Preise, Datenschutz, Aktualität und Grenzen.
methodology.intro: Jedes VPN wird in mehreren Testbereichen nach derselben standardisierten Methode bewertet. Werbeeinnahmen beeinflussen weder Rankings noch Bewertungen.

independence.title: 1. Independence and Revenue Disclosure
independence.intro: To earn your trust we openly disclose our revenue model. The site's revenue comes from Google AdSense ads; we receive no commission from any VPN provider.
independence.withAffiliateBody: The site's only revenue source is Google AdSense ads. We receive no sales commission from any VPN provider; links to providers are plain, non-commercial links that go directly to the brand's official site.
independence.withoutAffiliateBody: All providers, including Mullvad, are scored against the same criteria. Ad revenue does not influence rankings or scores — this is the most concrete signal of our impartiality.

pledgeItems.0: Every VPN subscription we test is purchased with our own money; we do not accept free or sponsored accounts from providers.
pledgeItems.1: No provider has pre-publication review, edit or veto rights over our content.
pledgeItems.2: Rankings, scores and critical notes are the responsibility of the editorial team; sales and marketing have no input.
pledgeItems.3: A provider's score is calculated independently of ad revenue; a brand running ads does not move it higher in the ranking.

independence.linkText: See the Advertising Disclosure page for full details.

tests.title: 2. Testing Methodology
tests.intro: Jedes Anbieterprofil wird anhand derselben Quellenstruktur in fünf Informationsbereichen eingeordnet. Die Kriterien stehen unten.

speed.title: a) Speed test
speed.summary: Measurements over the same baseline, with fixed hardware and ISP, across three geographic regions.
speed.tools: Ookla Speedtest CLI, Cloudflare speed.cloudflare.com (cross-verification), fast.com (CDN-based sanity check).
speed.locations: Turkey (Istanbul, near server), Germany (Frankfurt, medium distance), USA (New York, far distance).

methodSteps.0: Before any test we take 5 measurements with the VPN off and compute the baseline (download, upload, ping).
methodSteps.1: For each VPN we select the preferred protocol (WireGuard / Lightway / NordLynx).
methodSteps.2: On every server we take 10 measurements 60 seconds apart; the highest and lowest are discarded and the remaining 8 are averaged.
methodSteps.3: We run separate tests at a fixed off-peak time (09:00–11:00) and at peak (20:00–22:00).
methodSteps.4: Results are reported as the percentage drop versus baseline; raw speed alone is not meaningful.

speed.metrics: Download (Mbps), Upload (Mbps), Ping (ms), Jitter (ms), packet loss (%).

security.title: b) Security and leak tests
security.summary: Technical tests that verify how much protection a VPN really delivers.
security.tools: ipleak.net, dnsleaktest.com (extended test), browserleaks.com (WebRTC + canvas), test-ipv6.com, Wireshark (TCP-level packet inspection).

checks.0: IPv4 leak: whether the real IP is exposed while the VPN is active.
checks.1: IPv6 leak: many home connections have IPv6 enabled; does the provider block it?
checks.2: WebRTC-Leak: relevante Browser- und Plattformgrenzen werden getrennt dokumentiert.
checks.3: DNS leak: do queries go to the VPN's own resolver or to the ISP? Verified via the extended test across 6 different resolvers.
checks.4: Kill switch: the VPN process is forcefully killed during an active connection (Task Manager / kill -9) and we verify that internet access is actually severed.

security.config: We check whether the provider uses its own DNS, whether the default protocol is modern (WireGuard / OpenVPN UDP), the cipher (AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20) and certificate validation.

streaming.title: c) Streaming test
streaming.summary: How reliable is access to geo-restricted platforms?
streaming.platforms: Netflix (US, UK, JP, TR libraries), Disney+, BBC iPlayer, YouTube TV, Amazon Prime Video, BluTV and Exxen.

methodSteps.0: We log into each platform with our own paid subscription via parallel browser sessions.
methodSteps.1: Anbieterangaben zu regionaler Abdeckung und Servern werden anhand aktueller offizieller Dokumentation geprüft.
methodSteps.2: For providers that offer Smart DNS, obfuscated or streaming-optimised servers, standard and special servers are reported separately.
methodSteps.3: We also record video quality (480p / 1080p / 4K) and buffer time during the test.

streaming.result: Success rate per platform (%) — 9/9 working servers means 100%, none working means 0%.

privacy.title: d) Privacy and no-logs verification
privacy.summary: Evidence-based verification that goes beyond marketing claims.
privacy.audits: No-logs and application-security reports published by PwC, Deloitte, KPMG, Cure53, Securitum and Assured AB are read in their original form. The scope (servers, code or configuration), cadence and limitations of each report feed into the score.
privacy.jurisdiction: We review which 5/9/14-Eyes alliance the provider's home office belongs to, data-retention laws and history of legal compulsion. Jurisdictions like Panama, Switzerland and BVI are advantageous; the US and UK are disadvantageous.
privacy.policy: The privacy policy and terms are read end to end. Existence of a transparency report and a warrant canary is checked.
privacy.infra: Claims of RAM-only servers (no disks, everything wiped on reboot) are validated against provider documentation and independent reports.

usability.title: e) Usability, support and quality
usability.summary: The details that make daily use pleasant or painful.
usability.apps: Windows, macOS, iOS, Android and Linux apps are installed on real devices; install time, first connect time and UI ergonomics are documented.
usability.daily: Each VPN is used daily for at least 14 days: browsing, email, video calls, gaming and file transfer. Unstable connections, unexpected drops and battery drain are reported.
usability.support: We contact live chat at 3 different times (morning, afternoon, night). Response time, resolution quality and whether the agent actually has technical knowledge are evaluated.
usability.refund: Does the money-back guarantee really work? At the end of the test cycle we cancel the subscription and request a refund; we report whether the process is friction-free, how many days it takes and how much is actually refunded.

scoring.title: 3. Scoring System
scoring.intro: The results of the five test categories are mapped onto six scoring dimensions. Each dimension is rated 1–10 and contributes to the final score with the weights below.

security.name: Security
security.description: Leak-test results, kill-switch reliability, encryption standard, audit coverage.

privacy.name: Privacy
privacy.description: Jurisdiction, no-logs audits, RAM-only infrastructure, transparency report.

speed.name: Speed
speed.description: Percentage drop versus baseline; weighted average across three regions.

streaming.name: Streaming
streaming.description: Weighted average of per-platform success rates.

usability.name: Usability
usability.description: App quality, support response time, ease of first-time setup.

pricing.name: Pricing
pricing.description: Renewal-price transparency, true monthly cost, refund policy terms.

scoring.formula: Final score = Σ(dimension score × weight). Published as a decimal between 0.0 and 10.0.

freshness.title: 4. Freshness Policy
freshness.intro: The VPN market changes quickly. An independent audit may be strong evidence today and stale in two years. That is why we refresh our data regularly and display it transparently on every page.

items.0: Every VPN goes through the full test pipeline at least twice per year.
items.1: Jede Profilseite zeigt das relevante Quellen- und Preisprüfdatum deutlich an.
items.2: If a major event occurs (breach, ownership change, new audit, critical feature) we run an emergency re-test.
items.3: Pricing is tracked via a separate 'pricingVerifiedAt' field; we adapt to market price changes within 30 days.

transparency.title: 5. Transparency and Limitations

envItems.0: Hardware: Windows 11 (Intel i7, 32 GB RAM), MacBook Pro M2, Pixel 8 (Android 14), iPhone 15 (iOS 17).
envItems.1: ISP baseline: Türk Telekom fibre (1 Gbps down / 100 Mbps up).
envItems.3: Browsers: latest stable Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari.

limitsItems.0: Die Leistung hängt von ISP, Route, Serverlast und Gerät ab; feste Laborergebnisse veröffentlichen wir nicht.
limitsItems.1: Streaming success rates change over time — platforms continuously update their VPN detection.
limitsItems.2: Anbieterangaben und unabhängige Belege haben unterschiedliche Reichweiten; die Praxis kann abweichen.
limitsItems.3: We state explicitly that no independent certification body audits us; publishing our methodology openly is our strongest quality safeguard.
limitsItems.4: Users should make the final call based on their own priorities (privacy vs speed vs streaming).

transparency.contactBody: If you have a question or suggestion about the methodology, reach out via the contact page. If you find a serious error we verify it, update the affected page and publish a change note.

editorial.title: Editorial independence
editorial.body: We disclose our revenue model transparently (see <link>Advertising Disclosure</link>). The site's revenue comes from Google AdSense ads; we earn no commission from any VPN provider, which is the most direct signal of our impartiality.

privacy.title: Privacy policy and jurisdiction
privacy.body: We evaluate the provider's logging policy, the country its headquarters is in (5/9/14 Eyes alliances, data retention laws) and how it responds to legal requests.

audits.title: Independent audits
audits.body: The presence, frequency and scope of third-party audit reports (Deloitte, KPMG, Cure53, Securitum, Assured AB) drive the weight of this criterion.

speed.title: Speed
speed.body: Leistungsangaben werden anhand offizieller Technikdokumentation, Protokolldesigns und klarer Einschränkungen eingeordnet.

streaming.title: Streaming compatibility
streaming.body: Access tests on platforms like Netflix US/UK/TR, Disney+, BBC iPlayer, BluTV and Exxen using different servers.

pricing.title: Pricing transparency
pricing.body: The gap between the first-purchase price and the renewal price, hidden fees and the real money-back policy are all reviewed.

usability.title: Ease of use
usability.body: App interface, initial setup time, server-picker ergonomics and customer-support accessibility are all assessed.

calculator.ogDescription: Calculate the real 3-year VPN cost, renewal included.
calculator.intro: Most VPNs are cheap up front and expensive on renewal. Here you see the true 1/2/3-year total cost — compare fairly on "effective monthly" price.

tool.explanation: How it's calculated: discounted first-term price, then monthly-plan price on renewal. Most providers use a "renewal trap" — cheap up front, 2–3× more after. Disabling auto-renew and re-buying on discount saves money.

howSection.calcBody: For each VPN we take the "best value" plan (typically 2–3 years) as the reference. During the plan term the discounted price applies; after it expires we assume renewal at the monthly-plan rate. This is the source of most Trustpilot complaints — users see "$30 the first year, $120 the second year."
howSection.trapTitle: How to dodge the renewal trap
howSection.trap1Body: — log in to your VPN account and turn off auto-renew in billing settings.
howSection.trap2Body: buy a fresh discounted plan from the same provider or a different one.
howSection.trap3Body: — flat €5/month, no discount/renewal trap. Better for consistency than for squeezing out savings.
howSection.term1Body: The right balance for most users — meaningful discount, manageable commitment.
howSection.term2Body: Lowest effective monthly, but a 3-year commitment to one provider. The VPN market moves fast — even cheap is risky.
howSection.term3Body: Flexibility but 2–3× more expensive. Only for short-term needs.

about.lede: The VPN world is confusing: hundreds of providers, contradicting reviews, aggressive marketing. {site} started as a personal response to that mess — a volunteer review project.

explainer.title: What is this?
explainer.body: {site} is not a company or institution; it has no registered legal entity. It is a public version of the notes that built up while we were comparing VPN providers for our own use. Google AdSense ad revenue covers infrastructure costs; it does not influence the recommendations. See <disclosure>Advertising disclosure</disclosure> and <legal>Legal notice</legal> for details.

approach.body: Wir möchten klare, unabhängige und quellenbasierte Informationen zur VPN-Auswahl zugänglich machen. Unsere Einordnungen beruhen auf unabhängigen Auditberichten, öffentlichen Quellen und offizieller Dokumentation — nicht auf Marketingtexten. Keine Empfehlung ist eine Garantie; die Entscheidung bleibt bei Ihnen.

transparent.title: Transparent methodology
transparent.body: Every VPN is scored against the same six criteria. The criteria and their weights are public.

independence.title: Editorial independence
independence.body: Ad revenue does not influence the ranking or the assessment. We list all providers against the same criteria.

evidence.title: Evidence first
evidence.body: Saying "good VPN" isn't enough — independent audits, court rulings or audit reports are required.

howWeTest.body: Every VPN on the site is evaluated against the same six objective criteria: privacy policy and jurisdiction, independent audits, speed, streaming compatibility, pricing transparency and ease of use. See our <methodology>methodology page</methodology> for the details.

revenue.body1: We finance this site through Google AdSense ad revenue. Pages show ads served by Google; links to VPN providers are plain, non-commercial links and we earn no commission from them. We explain this in detail on the <disclosure>Advertising disclosure</disclosure> page.
revenue.body2: Important: Ad revenue does not influence the ranking. We rank all providers (including e.g. Mullvad) against the same criteria; a brand running ads does not get placed at the top.

authors.body: {site} started as a personal project. Content is produced through volunteer contributions; there is no professional newsroom or editorial staff. The primary sources are providers' own audit reports, publicly available court documents, open-source repositories and our own observations. If you find anything wrong or missing, please let us know — we take corrections seriously.

why.body: Commercial VPN reviews are mostly sales-driven; "best" claims get repeated without sources. {site} is a reference project that started as a hobby and grew more systematic over time, written into that gap. The goal is not to give a single "correct answer" — it's to provide structured information so the reader can make their own call.

emailSecurity.metaDescription: Prüfen Sie eine E-Mail-Adresse auf Domain-Sicherheitssignale: MX, SPF, DMARC, Wegwerfadresse-Risiko und optionale Have-I-Been-Pwned-Treffer. Kostenlos und datenschutzbewusst.
emailSecurity.title: E-Mail-Sicherheitscheck
emailSecurity.subtitle: Prüfen Sie, ob eine E-Mail-Adresse zu einer sauber geschützten Domain gehört und ob, falls konfiguriert, Have I Been Pwned Hinweise auf bekannte Datenlecks liefert.
emailSecurity.invalidEmail: Geben Sie eine gültige E-Mail-Adresse ein und versuchen Sie es erneut.
emailSecurity.errorTitle: Der E-Mail-Check konnte nicht abgeschlossen werden
emailSecurity.errorBody: Der Sicherheitscheck ist vorübergehend nicht verfügbar. Bitte versuchen Sie es gleich erneut.
emailSecurity.rateLimitedBody: Über diese Verbindung wurden zu viele Prüfungen angefragt. Bitte warten Sie eine Minute.
emailSecurity.privacyDetail: Ihre E-Mail wird nur für diese Prüfung verwendet und nicht gespeichert. MX-, SPF- und DMARC-Ergebnisse stammen aus Live-DNS-Abfragen. Leak-Checks laufen serverseitig (Have I Been Pwned wenn konfiguriert, sonst XposedOrNot); keine API-Schlüssel werden an den Browser gesendet.
emailSecurity.noFindings: Es wurden keine dringenden Probleme gefunden. Nutzen Sie weiterhin 2FA und vermeiden Sie Passwort-Wiederverwendung.

mx.title: MX-Einträge
mx.pass: Diese Domain kann E-Mails über konfigurierte Mailserver empfangen.
mx.fail: Es wurden keine MX-Einträge gefunden. Die Adresse kann möglicherweise keine E-Mails empfangen.

spf.title: SPF
spf.pass: SPF ist vorhanden und nutzt einen Durchsetzungsmechanismus.
spf.warning: SPF ist vorhanden, aber die Policy ist schwach oder unvollständig.
spf.fail: Kein SPF-Eintrag gefunden. Spoofing ist für diese Domain leichter.

dmarc.title: DMARC
dmarc.pass: DMARC ist mit quarantine oder reject konfiguriert.
dmarc.warning: DMARC ist vorhanden, überwacht mit p=none aber nur.
dmarc.fail: Keine DMARC-Policy gefunden. Der Phishing-Schutz ist schwächer.

breach.clear: In der Leak-Datenbank wurde für diese Adresse kein bekannter Eintrag gefunden.
breach.found: Diese Adresse erscheint in einem oder mehreren bekannten Datenlecks.
breach.unavailable: Die Leak-Datenbank antwortet vorübergehend nicht. MX-, SPF- und DMARC-Ergebnisse stammen aus Live-DNS-Abfragen.

findings.breach_found: Ändern Sie das Passwort für diese E-Mail und alle Konten, in denen dasselbe Passwort genutzt wurde. Aktivieren Sie 2FA für wichtige Konten.
findings.hibp_not_configured: Leak-Datenbank-Check ist derzeit nicht verfügbar; MX-, SPF- und DMARC-Ergebnisse sind dennoch Live-DNS-Abfragen.
findings.hibp_unavailable: Die Leak-Datenbank war nicht erreichbar. Führen Sie die Prüfung später erneut aus.
findings.no_mx: Die Domain hat keine MX-Einträge. Prüfen Sie die Adresse oder nutzen Sie eine andere E-Mail.
findings.no_spf: Bitten Sie den Domaininhaber, SPF einzurichten, damit gefälschte Absender schwerer werden.
findings.weak_spf: Verschärfen Sie die SPF-Policy und vermeiden Sie permissive Mechanismen wie +all.
findings.no_dmarc: Fügen Sie DMARC zunächst im Monitoring hinzu und wechseln Sie danach zu quarantine oder reject.
findings.dmarc_monitor_only: DMARC läuft nur im Monitoring. Wechseln Sie nach Auswertung der Reports zu quarantine oder reject.
findings.disposable_email: Wegwerf-E-Mail-Domains sind für wichtige Konten riskant. Nutzen Sie ein dauerhaftes Postfach.
findings.role_account: Rollenadressen werden oft geteilt. Nutzen Sie eindeutige Benutzer, starke Passwörter und 2FA.

emailSecurity.explainBody: Das Tool validiert das E-Mail-Format, prüft MX-, SPF- und DMARC-Einträge der Domain per Live-DNS, markiert häufige Wegwerf- oder Rollenadressen und sucht in Leak-Datenbanken (Have I Been Pwned wenn konfiguriert, sonst XposedOrNot). Die Ergebnisse sind keine Simulation.

dns.metaTitle: DNS Leak Test 2026 - Free | VPN Advisor
dns.metaDescription: Is your VPN leaking DNS? Use our free browser-based test to see your DNS resolvers and protect your privacy.
dns.title: DNS Leak Test
dns.subtitle: Even with a VPN on, your DNS queries might still go to your ISP. This test reveals which resolver you actually use.
dns.experimentalTitle: Experimental tool — does not test your system DNS
dns.experimentalBody: This test queries directly over Cloudflare DoH (1.1.1.1); it does not measure your operating system's actual DNS resolver. For a reliable DNS leak test use a server-side tool such as dnsleaktest.com. Below are the resolvers Cloudflare reported.
dns.noLeakBody: Your DNS queries go through a single resolver. If you use a VPN, make sure it belongs to your provider.
dns.leakBody: Multiple distinct resolvers detected. Your ISP can still see the sites you visit.
dns.explainTitle: What is a DNS leak, why is it dangerous?
dns.explainBody: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses. Even when you use a VPN, misconfiguration can route DNS queries to your ISP, exposing your browsing history.

webrtc.metaTitle: WebRTC Leak Test - Is Your Real IP Exposed? | VPN Advisor
webrtc.metaDescription: WebRTC can leak your real IP even with a VPN on. Use this free browser test to check.
webrtc.title: WebRTC Leak Test
webrtc.subtitle: WebRTC powers video calls in your browser. Unfortunately, it can leak your real IP even when your VPN is on.
webrtc.noLeakBody: Your public IP is not exposed through WebRTC. Your browser is well configured.
webrtc.leakBody: WebRTC is exposing your public IP. Sites can see your real location even with a VPN.
webrtc.fixChrome: Chrome: install the WebRTC Network Limiter extension.
webrtc.fixFirefox: Firefox: open about:config and set media.peerconnection.enabled to false.
webrtc.fixBrave: Brave: Settings > Privacy > WebRTC IP handling policy = Default Public Interface Only.

speed.metaTitle: VPN Speed Test - Free Internet Speed Check 2026 | VPN Advisor
speed.metaDescription: Measure your VPN's real speed. Test download speed and latency using Cloudflare infrastructure.
speed.title: VPN Speed Test
speed.subtitle: Turn on your VPN before running this test. Run it again with the VPN off and compare.
speed.error: The speed test could not complete. Check your connection and try again — some corporate networks or ad blockers may block the Cloudflare test server.
speed.embedNote: For a more in-depth test use Cloudflare's official tool.
speed.explainTitle: How much speed loss with a VPN is normal?
speed.explainBody: A VPN encrypts your traffic and routes it through a remote server. A 10-30% speed drop is typical. If you lose more than 50%, switch servers or try another protocol (WireGuard is usually fastest).
